label: The 1929 riots
note: Communal violence from Jerusalem outward; 133 Jews and 116 Arabs killed across the country. Haifa saw far less than Hebron or Safed, but the year is the hinge on which Mandate communal policy turned.

label: St. Luke's mission hospital closes
note: The Church Missionary Society hospital on Mountain Road shuts. Its premises are the ones the Government later rents; the register opens in them in 1930.

label: Passfield White Paper
note: Restricts Jewish immigration and land purchase in the wake of the Shaw and Hope Simpson reports; effectively withdrawn by the MacDonald Letter of Feb 1931.

label: The Fifth Aliyah
note: The largest wave of the Mandate: roughly 200,000 arrivals 1932-1938, most in these four years, driven by the Nazi seizure of power. Haifa is the port of entry and its population roughly doubles in the decade.
source: Survey of Palestine (1946), vol. I ch. VI

label: The Jaffa demonstrations
note: Arab general strike and demonstrations against immigration; police fire on crowds in Jaffa and Haifa. Among the first mass casualty events of the decade in Haifa itself.

label: The Haavara Agreement
note: Transfer agreement enabling German Jews to move capital to Palestine as goods; underwrites much of the Fifth Aliyah's German component.

label: Drought and the water crisis
note: A severe dry year across the country; typhoid and dysentery seasons are reported worse than usual.
source: Report to the Council of the League of Nations, 1934

label: Haifa harbour opens
note: The deep-water port is inaugurated after five years of construction, remaking the city's labour market and its population.
source: Report to the Council of the League of Nations, 1933

label: The IPC pipeline reaches Haifa
note: The Iraq Petroleum Company line from Kirkuk terminates at Haifa; the refinery follows. Industrial injury enters the city's casualty pattern.
source: Report to the Council of the League of Nations, 1935

label: Izz al-Din al-Qassam killed
note: The Haifa-based preacher is killed by police in the hills; his funeral in Haifa becomes a mass demonstration, and his death is generally read as a trigger of the Revolt.
source: Survey of Palestine (1946), vol. I ch. II

label: The Arab Revolt
note: Three years of general strike, armed insurgency and British counter-insurgency. Haifa, its port and the refinery are repeatedly attacked; the Government Hospital is built through the whole of it.
source: Survey of Palestine (1946), vol. I ch. II

label: The general strike
note: The Revolt's first phase: a six-month Arab general strike, with Haifa port at its centre.

label: The Peel Commission reports partition
note: Recommends partitioning Palestine, with Haifa in the proposed Jewish state under temporary British mandate. Rejected by the Arab leadership; the Revolt resumes in September.

label: The Haifa market bombings
note: A series of bombings in the Arab market of Haifa, among the deadliest single incidents of the Revolt; scores killed and many more wounded, and the wounded go to the Government Hospital.

label: The MacDonald White Paper
note: Caps Jewish immigration at 75,000 over five years and restricts land transfer; the frame for the illegal-immigration years that follow.

label: The Second World War
note: Palestine becomes a rear base and, from 1940, a target. Military demand reshapes the Government Hospital's beds and staff.

label: Italian air raid on Haifa
note: Italian aircraft bomb the port and refinery area; dozens killed. The first of a series of raids on the city in 1940-1941.

label: The heaviest raid on Haifa
note: Italian bombing of the Haifa oil installations and adjacent quarters, the war's worst single day of civilian casualties in the city.

label: The Patria sinks in Haifa bay
note: The Haganah's charge intended to disable the deportation ship sinks it in the harbour; over 250 refugees and crew drown, and the survivors are landed at Haifa.

label: Atlit detention camp in use
note: Intercepted ma'apilim are held at the camp south of Haifa. Notebook 25 of this register is the camp's own admission book for 1940.

label: The Struma sinks
note: The refugee ship, refused entry to Palestine, is torpedoed after being towed from Istanbul; one survivor of some 780. A turning point in Mandate immigration politics.

label: Plague years in Palestine
note: Bubonic plague is reported in the country, with Haifa among the affected districts; the Government Hospital's plague department dates from 1942.
source: Annual Report of the Department of Health, 1944

label: Bevin announces the Anglo-American Committee
note: Immigration remains capped; the announcement is followed by riots in Tel Aviv and elsewhere.

label: Black Sabbath
note: Mass British arrests and searches across the country against the Jewish Agency and the Haganah.

label: The King David Hotel bombing
note: The Irgun destroys the hotel's south wing; 91 killed. Followed by curfews and searches in Haifa among other cities.

label: The Exodus 1947 is brought into Haifa
note: The intercepted immigrant ship is escorted into Haifa port; the wounded are landed and the rest deported back to Europe. The register's 1947 notebooks cover these weeks.

label: The UN partition resolution
note: Resolution 181 recommends partition; fighting begins in the country within days and does not stop.

label: The Haifa refinery killings
note: An Irgun bomb at the refinery gate is followed by the killing of Jewish refinery workers by Arab workers, and by reprisals. Among the deadliest days in the city's own war.

label: The battle for Haifa
note: Haganah operation Bi'ur Hametz takes the city over two days; the Arab population largely leaves by sea and road. The register's last notebook stops in these weeks.
source: Survey of Palestine and contemporary press

label: The Mandate ends
note: The British administration withdraws; the State of Israel is declared. The Government Hospital passes to the municipality on 2 May.
